purpose: Install headroom-ai==0.38.0 (mcp extra) into a NEW isolated uv-tool prefix alongside the pinned 0.37.0, read its actual CLI/MCP docs, and run the same guarded MCP compress/retrieve recovery check the 0.37.0 receipt ran, to settle whether the pin_behind_upstream flag on token-efficiency gap 2 is safe to advance.
fix_round_disclosure: A first attempt at this check (blueprints/gap-resolution-20260922/headroom-0.38.0-recovery/run.sh, results below under corrected_procedure.superseded_invalid_run) was found NOT isolated: it set only UV_TOOL_DIR/UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR/UV_PYTHON for the uv install, but the `headroom mcp serve` process it launched omitted HEADROOM_WORKSPACE_DIR, HEADROOM_OFFLINE and HEADROOM_TELEMETRY. Running it wrote into the live default Headroom store at ~/.headroom (ccr_store.db modified, session_stats.jsonl created with this run's compress/retrieve events, sub_agents.compressions=1/retrievals=1) and made an online update check (update_check.json created with {"latest_version": "0.38.0"}). The pinned 0.37.0 install binary itself was not touched, but its default store was. That first receipt also overclaimed: its fixture (fixtures/rag-note.md, 351 bytes / 75 tokens) only ever triggered Headroom's no-op router (tokens_saved 0), so it demonstrated a store/fetch round trip of unchanged content, not the compression-recovery behavior the 0.37.0 receipt (mcp_compact_json_baseline 36625 -> mcp_candidate_summary 19714) actually exercised, even though the receipt's own preregistered rule and verdict_impact treated it as settling recovery. Per the fix-round rule that a wrong procedure may be re-run once with a new preregistration, this receipt now records BOTH the original invalid run (disclosed, not deleted, not used to settle anything) and one corrected, isolated re-run with a fixture that does trigger a compressing transform. The ~/.headroom entries the invalid run wrote were left in place: removing them required explicit coordinator authorization that this fix round did not grant.
preregistered: Corrected procedure (superseded_invalid_run is retained only as a disclosed defect record and settles nothing): with HEADROOM_WORKSPACE_DIR set to a disposable directory under codex-ecosystem's gap-resolution-20260922/token-observation scratch path, HEADROOM_OFFLINE=1 and HEADROOM_TELEMETRY=off, and a larger owned synthetic fixture shaped like the 0.37.0 receipt's MCP-tool-listing fixture (blueprints/gap-resolution-20260922/headroom-0.38.0-recovery/mcp-tool-listing.json, an owned synthetic MCP tools/list-shaped JSON document, not captured production traffic), if headroom_compress on 0.38.0 selects a transform other than router:noop (i.e. exercises real compression, not just storage) and headroom_retrieve returns byte-for-byte original content (sha256 match), and the disposable HEADROOM_WORKSPACE_DIR store (not ~/.headroom) receives the write, then the pin_behind_upstream flag can advance from 0.37.0 to 0.38.0 as a safe upgrade candidate for this recovery property specifically. If recovery is inexact, the MCP tool errors, the transform is still a no-op despite the larger fixture, or ~/.headroom is touched again, the pin stays at 0.37.0 and the discrepancy is recorded honestly. This check still does not exercise the proxy-intercept path (proxy target 127.0.0.1:1 is intentionally unreachable, matching both the 0.37.0 receipt's and the first 0.38.0 attempt's fixtures) and does not touch the live 0.37.0 install.

result: Corrected, isolated re-run: HEADROOM_WORKSPACE_DIR pointed at a disposable directory (not ~/.headroom), HEADROOM_OFFLINE=1 and HEADROOM_TELEMETRY=off were set on the MCP server process, and the check used a larger owned synthetic fixture (blueprints/gap-resolution-20260922/headroom-0.38.0-recovery/mcp-tool-listing.json, 183,628 bytes / 39,064 tokens, an MCP tools/list-shaped JSON document) instead of the original small rag-note.md fixture. headroom_compress selected transform 'router:mixed:0.09' (not router:noop), reducing 39,064 tokens to 3,292 (91.6% savings) -- this is real compression, unlike the original run. headroom_retrieve then returned content that matched the original byte-for-byte (sha256 2b17eb36da607cc8d2f6f0e2802193c0a0587ffbae361e667d093930d3a5533d on both sides). headroom_stats on this disposable workspace showed exactly 1 compression / 1 retrieval / 35,772 tokens_saved, confirming no cross-contamination from the earlier disclosed invalid run (whose artifacts were removed from the disposable workspace directory before this run, though its writes to the live ~/.headroom store were left in place per the no-unauthorized-cleanup instruction). Pre- and post-run stat of ~/.headroom's three files showed byte-identical mtimes, and no update_check.json appeared in the disposable workspace, confirming this corrected run neither touched the live store nor made an online update check. The mcporter 0.13.13 CLI itself has a parsing defect unrelated to Headroom: it silently drops a lone `key=@path` positional argument by mis-consuming it as a server/tool 'selector' when --tool is already given by flag (reproduced with both the small and large fixtures, and confirmed by reading mcporter's own call-arguments.js); a leading dummy positional token works around it. Separately, the 0.38.0 CLI help continues to confirm the critic's original correction that there is no `headroom compress` CLI subcommand (only audit-reads/evals/inspect/mcp/savings), unchanged from the first (invalid) run's finding on that point, which is retained below for completeness.

verdict_impact.explanation: With isolation fixed and a fixture that actually exercises headroom's compressing transform (router:mixed, 91.6% reduction on this fixture) rather than the no-op path, exact MCP compress/retrieve recovery holds on 0.38.0, and the CLI-surface shape (no compress subcommand) still matches the critic's correction. This now more robustly supports advancing the pin_behind_upstream flag from 0.37.0 to 0.38.0 than the invalid first run did. It only partially settles gap 2 because: (1) blueprints/gap-resolution-20260922/headroom-0.38.0-recovery/mcp-tool-listing.json is an owned synthetic reconstruction shaped like an MCP tool listing, not the exact fixture the 0.37.0 receipt used, so the two receipts' compression-ratio numbers (91.6% here vs 46.2% there) are not a strict apples-to-apples comparison of 0.37.0 vs 0.38.0 compression behavior, only of exact-recovery correctness on each version's own fixture; (2) the proxy-intercept path remains unexercised by design in every receipt in this lineage; (3) the live ~/.headroom store still carries the disclosed contamination from the invalid first run, which was left in place pending coordinator authorization rather than settled by this receipt.
verdict_impact.corrects_prior_receipt: This receipt's prior version (same id, same date, before this fix round) said 'nothing here blocks advancing the pin_behind_upstream flag' based on a no-op storage round trip and did not disclose that its own MCP server process had written to the live ~/.headroom store. That prior verdict_impact text is superseded by this one; both defects (isolation and the noop-fixture overclaim) are now disclosed and corrected in the same receipt rather than filed separately.

limitations: The compression-ratio comparison between this run (91.6% on blueprints/gap-resolution-20260922/headroom-0.38.0-recovery/mcp-tool-listing.json) and the 0.37.0 receipt (46.2% on its own MCP-listing fixture) is not apples-to-apples: the fixtures are different documents built at different times, so only exact-recovery correctness (not relative compression efficiency across versions) is directly comparable.

The configured Headroom proxy (127.0.0.1:1) was unreachable by design in every receipt in this lineage (0.37.0, the invalid first 0.38.0 run, and this corrected run), so automatic proxy-intercept compression has never been exercised by any of them.

The disclosed contamination of the live ~/.headroom store (ccr_store.db, session_stats.jsonl, update_check.json) from the first, invalid run was NOT reverted by this receipt; the fix-round task required explicit coordinator authorization to remove those entries, which was not granted in this round, so they remain a known, disclosed side effect pending that authorization.

Only one corrected MCP round-trip (compress+retrieve+stats) was run once as preregistered, per the fix-round rule against re-running to fish for a different outcome; no retry or alternate-fixture rerun was performed beyond this single corrected procedure.

Individual MCP call durations were not precisely instrumented (each completed well under its 60s command timeout); duration_s values for those three commands are approximate, unchanged from the invalid run's receipt.

The installed wheel's sha256 was not independently recomputed in this fix round (the 0.38.0 install itself was reused unmodified from the invalid run, since installation was not implicated by either finding); it remains recorded from PyPI's published JSON API digest for the matching platform tag.

mcporter 0.13.13's positional-argument selector-consumption defect (see result) is a client-side CLI quirk this receipt worked around with a dummy positional token; it was not reported upstream as part of this task and is not itself evidence about Headroom.
